# Glimmer Scene backend integration

Pinned upstream: `8d9e86d16e87395d0ab46710b05ecc24fd992539` (GPL-3.0 repository; nested dependency licenses retained). This isolated copy derives from the frozen research patch recorded in `GLIMMER-PROVENANCE.json`. Private Wallpaper Engine assets and user projects are not included. Original Glimmer code retains its own MIT notices; distribution of the GPL helper/framework must preserve the applicable GPL notices and corresponding source.

The native app compiles only `Sources/SceneBackendShared/SceneBackendTypes.swift`. It does not link this framework. The separate XPC executable imports the public `SceneBackendFacade` from a Release framework built with `ENABLE_TESTABILITY=NO`.

`SceneBackendFacade.prepare(configuration)` installs an explicit once-per-process runtime context before upstream services initialize. Configuration names read roots for a packed or loose Scene project and verified official assets, plus a private mode-0700 cache root. Project JSON digest is checked by the helper; the assets manifest identity is supplied after the host registry verifies the complete dataset. No discovery of default Workshop roots or dependency links is permitted. Memory settings, in-process shader compilation, isolated script storage, and repository-owned Metal source replace app-global storage/helper relaunch paths.

The facade exposes `readiness`, `render(input)`, `acknowledge(token)`, `setPaused`, `updateProperties`, and `close`. Preparation fails closed unless positive authored-object, original resource, font, video, script, pipeline and completed-GPU-frame evidence passes the generic readiness collector. Failed readiness evidence remains in the explicit cache's `readiness.json`. Sound and unaudited capabilities are rejected. Shortcuts, media-session monitoring, system audio capture, global clicks, and default app migrations are not started. User texture paths must resolve inside the explicit project root. Backend video is muted; attempted dynamic sound/video-audio use records a fatal runtime error.

A frame transfers an IOSurface capability through NSXPC after successful GPU completion. Production rendering never reads pixels back to CPU. The three-slot BGRA pool does not overwrite any published surface until its exact session/generation/sequence/slot token is acknowledged after the host GPU finishes sampling. The host should have one render request in flight per session. Rejected/stale inputs do not establish readiness; transport backpressure requires a later sequence number. Cursor coordinates use output pixels with bottom-left origin; clicks are currently unsupported.

Connections to one XPC service identifier share a process. `SceneBackendServiceCatalog` defines eight explicit bundle identifiers; each active Scene must own a distinct service identifier. One connection owns a helper session; additional connections may inspect PID/instance status but cannot acquire/control that session. The host must wait for close/process exit before reusing a slot. Invalidation cleans and exits the owner process. No global runtime reset or cross-project singleton reuse is attempted.

Build with `scripts/build-scene-backend.sh`. Generated services live below the explicit build output; embed all eight under the host's `Contents/XPCServices`, with the single framework and Sparkle dependency under `Contents/Frameworks`. Required package resource bundles are copied into each helper's Resources. The script uses runtime public Metal source compilation because this machine lacks the optional offline Metal toolchain; it does not install Xcode components. `SCENE_BACKEND_BUILD_PROBE=YES` uses the existing stable certificate-backed identity to build a self-owned non-GUI probe bundle for isolated acceptance only, never a normal upstream app.

Filesystem containment and service authentication are explicit code guards, not an OS sandbox claim. A separately reviewed sandbox/hardened-runtime deployment and final signed bundle tests remain packaging gates. Functional success for the two original projects does not establish Windows pixel equivalence, desktop-seam equivalence, or universal Scene compatibility.

Original-resource readiness checks use the same loader VFS as rendering: package entries, then project loose files, then the explicit engine assets. Package resource names retain every internal space. Missing, unsafe or oversized resources still fail readiness; no loose expansion or author-file edits are required.
